abstract: Maintains runway icing condition assessments and transit corridor altitude profiles
system_message:
You are the Aviation Meteorology Lead (MET). Your business responsibilities include maintaining runway icing condition assessments and transit corridor altitude profiles, as well as providing severe turbulence forecasting for alpine evacuation routes.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Severe turbulence forecasting（TURB）
information_points.content:
MET-TURB-YAH：For the Valley River Low-Altitude Transit, Doppler radar profiling records a peak mountain-wave gust velocity of 50 kt across the en-route mountain pass sectors.
MET-TURB-VNJ：For the Glacier Pass High-Level Route, Doppler radar profiling indicates a peak mountain-wave gust velocity of 65 kt within the en-route mountain pass sectors.
MET-TURB-O55：For the Southern Crest Ridge Bypass, Doppler radar profiling projects a peak mountain-wave gust velocity of 35 kt across the en-route mountain pass sectors.

information_points.title: Maintains runway icing condition assessments and transit corridor altitude profiles（CLIM）
information_points.content:
MET-CLIM-Z4G：For the Glacier Pass High-Level Route, forward runway de-icing clearance is confirmed as true for the staging airstrip runway, and the transit corridor en-route clearance altitude across the mountainous flight path is 4600 m.
MET-CLIM-SI6：For the Valley River Low-Altitude Transit, forward runway de-icing clearance is confirmed as true for the staging airstrip runway, while the transit corridor en-route clearance altitude along the mountainous corridor is 3800 m.
MET-CLIM-8RB：For the Southern Crest Ridge Bypass, forward runway de-icing clearance is confirmed as true for the staging airstrip runway, and the transit corridor en-route clearance altitude across the mountainous transit corridor is 5000 m.
